clue.text: Almost from the start, just horrid

indicators.note: nearly whole, with the shortfall at the front, so the opening letter of the word is dropped

blocks.note: just in the sense of within the law

explanation.surface: Someone has been simply horrid almost from the beginning of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just' looks like the adverb meaning merely, but it is the adjective meaning fair or legal; LAWFUL loses its L.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something very unpleasant or dreadful, so they are straightforward synonyms.

clue.text: Noodles topped as agreed

indicators.note: in a down entry, having its top cut off means losing the opening letter

explanation.surface: Noodles were garnished on top just as had been arranged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topped' suggests garnished, but it means beheaded: RAMEN without its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Said at the end of a prayer, the word expresses assent, so it signals that something is so agreed.

clue.text: Consumer hassled Netflix about opera content

indicators.note: something hassled is harried and thrown into disorder, so the letters get rearranged
about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go around the other piece

blocks.note: an aria is a solo song found within an opera

explanation.surface: A customer pesters a streaming service about its opera programming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Consumer' reads as a TV viewer, but it is an eater: a FLEXITARIAN is a mostly vegetarian diner who sometimes eats meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A flexitarian is a kind of eater with a largely plant-based diet, and an eater is literally a consumer of food.

clue.text: Hang around, from "chill" in German

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows, spanning their boundaries

blocks.note: the run spans the end of chill, all of in and the start of German

explanation.surface: A word meaning to hang around is said to come from the German for chill.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make it look like an etymology note, but the answer sits in plain view inside the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To linger is to stay somewhere longer than needed, which is what hanging around means.

clue.text: Is it a chop stewing? That should be roasted!

indicators.note: stewing in a pot jumbles the ingredients, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A cook objects that a chop is being stewed when it ought to have been roasted.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about cooking a chop; the definition is the exclamation, describing a nut that is usually sold roasted.
explanation.definitionFit: Pistachio nuts are typically roasted and salted before eating, so the exclamation describes one cryptically.

clue.text: Pleasant friend engaged in fit

blocks.note: an informal word for a mate
busy with something, as in at work or at play
fit in the sense of capable

explanation.surface: A pleasant friend has got involved in a fit of temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engaged in' looks like a container signal, but here it supplies AT, as in being at something.
explanation.definitionFit: Palatable means agreeable to the taste or to the mind, so it is a synonym of acceptable or pleasant.

clue.text: Sting or En Vogue?

blocks.note: first meaning: to hurt with a sharp burning pain

explanation.walkthrough: Sting and En Vogue are both pop acts, so the clue looks like a music quiz; each is really an ordinary word.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the answer means to cause a sharp pain; as an adjective it means fashionable or well dressed.

clue.text: French spin on insalata

indicators.note: a spin on something is a new version of it, so the letters are put in a fresh order

blocks.note: Italian for salad, taken as written

explanation.surface: A chef offers a French take on the Italian salad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French' is an adjective meaning from France; an Alsatian is someone or something from Alsace, a French region.
explanation.definitionFit: Alsace is a region of eastern France, so anything Alsatian is French in origin.

clue.text: Female pronoun -- new?

explanation.surface: A query about whether a new pronoun for women has been coined.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface nods to the Swedish gender-neutral pronoun hen; the masculine pronoun is the irony.
explanation.definitionFit: A hen is a female bird, and the word is also used for female animals such as fish or lobsters.

clue.text: Wipe out old book before reading

explanation.surface: Someone erases an old book before anyone has had a chance to read it.
explanation.definitionFit: To obliterate is to destroy completely, leaving no trace, which is what wiping out means.

clue.text: Going on outside having deleted social media app

indicators.note: something deleted is removed, so one piece is taken out of the word

explanation.surface: Someone is out and about, having removed a social media app from their phone.
explanation.walkthrough: X is the current name of Twitter; removing it from EXTERNAL leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternal means lasting forever, so it describes something that just keeps going on.

clue.text: Side roads backed up on Axminster's outskirts

indicators.note: the outskirts of a town are its edges, so only the outer letters of the word are used
backing up means going in reverse, so the word is read from right to left

blocks.note: the first and last letters of the town's name

explanation.surface: Traffic on the side roads queues back towards the edge of the Devon town of Axminster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Side' is a sports team: Arsenal is a London football club. Axminster is a town in Devon famous for carpets.
explanation.definitionFit: A side is a team in sport, and Arsenal is a well-known English football team.

clue.text: Two papers grasp to renounce putting fool in online issue

indicators.note: to grasp is to hold, so the newspapers go around what follows
putting one thing into another places it inside, with the word in completing the instruction

blocks.note: the i, a British daily, and the FT, the Financial Times

explanation.surface: Two newspapers refuse to call someone an idiot over an internet problem.
explanation.walkthrough: The i and the FT are British newspapers; the second is written with its article, THE FT, and the pair split to hold the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealing someone's personal details is a common crime on the internet, so it is a problem that arises online.

clue.text: Huge football legend turned funny, tangled in net

indicators.note: turned round means facing the other way, so the name is written backwards
tangled things are knotted out of order, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A great footballer goes comic, getting tangled up in the goal net.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is part of the jumbled letters, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Elephantine means as big as an elephant, so it is a figurative word for huge or enormous.

clue.text: Collapsing grocery chain admits extremely louche image

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the store name holds the next piece
the extremes of a word are its ends, so its first and last letters are used

blocks.note: first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A failing supermarket chain lets in a seedy picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collapsing' looks like the failing business, but it is the definition: a telescopic aerial slides into itself. Tesco is Britain's biggest supermarket chain.
explanation.definitionFit: Telescopic parts slide inside one another to shorten, just as a collapsing umbrella or aerial does.

clue.text: Say what gets publicity, I say

blocks.note: say in the sense of for example

explanation.surface: A question about what attracts attention in the media.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I say' is an old-fashioned British exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Egad is a dated mild oath expressing surprise, just like the exclamation I say.

clue.text: Pirate misheard the price of piercings in the US?

indicators.note: a phrase that is misheard is taken for something sounding the same

blocks.clueFragment: the price of piercings in the US
blocks.note: a buck is an American dollar, charged per ear pierced

explanation.surface: A pirate gets the cost of American ear piercing wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: A buck is US slang for a dollar, so a dollar per ear is a buck an ear.
explanation.definitionFit: Buccaneers were pirates who raided Spanish shipping in the Caribbean in the seventeenth century.

clue.text: Singing, hat-wearing, tin-carrying sailor

indicators.note: a hat that is worn sits round the head, so the headgear goes around the sailor

blocks.note: dated British slang for a hat

explanation.surface: A sailor in a hat sings while carrying a tin.
explanation.walkthrough: Tile is old slang for a hat; the tin leads, followed by the hat around the sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Cantabile is a musical direction meaning in a smooth, singing style, so it is the musical term for singing.

clue.text: Winger choking over in Bundesliga is 2 for 8

indicators.note: something choking grips around a throat, so the bird surrounds the next piece

blocks.note: a winger is a bird; the coot is a water bird
the German word for over, appropriate in the German football league

explanation.surface: A wide player in the German league is choking, and some numbers are reported.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' looks like a footballer, but it is any bird. The Bundesliga is the German league, so 'over' is put into German.
explanation.definitionFit: Two multiplied by itself three times is eight, so two is the number whose cube is eight.

clue.text: Impressive server hugs each foodie

indicators.note: to hug is to wrap your arms around, so the server encloses the next piece

explanation.surface: A wonderful waiter embraces every food lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'server' suggests a waiter, but it is an urn that serves tea.
explanation.definitionFit: An epicurean is a person devoted to refined food and drink, which is what a foodie is.

clue.text: Cropped George Michael group tee, eh?

indicators.note: cropped means cut short, so the final letter is trimmed off

blocks.note: the 1980s pop duo George Michael fronted

explanation.surface: Someone queries a cropped T-shirt from a George Michael band, the famous Choose Life tee.
explanation.walkthrough: Wham! was George Michael's 1980s duo, famous for slogan T-shirts.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are interjections asking someone to repeat what they said because it was not heard.

clue.text: Turnip oddly seen in jail crab meat

indicators.note: taking the odd-numbered positions, first, third, fifth and so on

blocks.note: letters one, three, five and onward of the phrase

explanation.surface: A turnip is spotted, oddly, in the crab meat served in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Jicama is a Mexican root vegetable often called the Mexican turnip or yam bean.

clue.text: Thinking hard criminal certain not to reform

indicators.note: reforming means being reshaped, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A criminal is sure not to mend their ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' looks like an adjective, but it is the noun giving a convict.
explanation.definitionFit: Concentration is the act of focusing the mind intensely on something, which is what thinking hard means.

clue.text: Last to accept pickled ham

indicators.note: the final letter belonging to the next word is the one used

blocks.note: pickled and high are both slang for intoxicated

explanation.surface: Someone is the last to agree to eat pickled ham.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ham' as a cut of meat is the rear leg of a pig.
explanation.definitionFit: Ham is meat from the upper part of a pig's hind leg, which is that animal's thigh.

clue.text: Material was touching

blocks.note: first meaning: a matted woollen cloth
second meaning: past tense of a verb for touching with the hand

explanation.walkthrough: 'was touching' reads as emotionally moving, but it means handled.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names a pressed woollen fabric, and the verb's past tense means having touched or handled something.

clue.text: Russian prince repelled by pasty dumplings

indicators.note: something repelled is driven back, so the name is turned round

blocks.note: a pasty is a pastry pie
Prince Igor, subject of Borodin's opera

explanation.surface: A Russian prince is put off by some pale, pasty dumplings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pasty' looks like the adjective pale, but it is the noun, a Cornish pasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierogi are filled dumplings from Eastern Europe, especially Poland, so the plural matches.

clue.text: Primate shedding its exterior layer

indicators.note: losing the outside means the first and last letters come off

explanation.surface: A primate is moulting its outer coat of fur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exterior layer' reads as a coat, but 'layer' is the definition: something that lays eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: The emu is a large bird, and every bird that lays eggs can be called a layer.

clue.text: When king's out for drink, I make believe

indicators.note: one letter goes out and something else comes in its place

explanation.surface: A child plays pretend, swapping the king for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make believe' looks like the definition, but 'make' belongs to the wordplay and only 'believe' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: To imagine can mean to suppose or think something is so, as in I imagine so, the same as believe.

clue.text: Low-cut accessory tour chose in error

indicators.note: a mistaken arrangement means the letters end up in a different order

explanation.surface: A revealing item was picked by mistake on a tour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low-cut' suggests a plunging neckline, but it describes a shoe; a court shoe is the British name for a plain pump.
explanation.definitionFit: A court shoe is a low-cut women's shoe without fastening, a fashion accessory called a pump in America.

clue.text: Facing bit of traffic, swear head off

indicators.note: a small bit of a word here means just its opening letter

explanation.surface: A driver stuck in traffic curses wildly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swear head off' looks like cursing heavily, but 'head off' is the definition, meaning prevent.
explanation.definitionFit: To avert a danger is to prevent or turn it away, which is what heading it off means.
